objective: Test whether reproducing the accepted R90 two-kernel GDN norm structure repairs c1 while preserving fixed row ownership and c2 invariance.

source_evidence.r96_observation: Two reduction warps restored R90's c2 behavior but left c1 exactly on R94's known-bad sequence.
source_evidence.interpretation: The remaining causal candidates are the intermediate FP32 row-sum store/load boundary and the separate four-warp pointwise stage. R97 changes both together because that is the exact generated structural unit under test.

change_from_r94: Replace the fused per-row norm-and-gate kernel with a dedicated one-program-per-row FP32 sum-of-squares kernel using two warps.
Write row sums to an FP32 temporary tensor.
Apply mean, epsilon, rsqrt, weight, SiLU gate, and output conversion in a separate four-warp pointwise kernel.

fixed_workload.sequence: Run cache-c000 alone at c1, then cache-c000 plus index-c001 at c2 on one fresh server and empty compile cache.

followup_if_pass: Build a non-tracing image and repeat c1/c2, then perform a clean-boot full varied-prompt qualification before performance measurement.
followup_if_fail: Preserve the result and separately sweep the pointwise launch block or match the generated persistent-reduction XBLOCK while retaining fixed row ownership.
promotion_boundary: Diagnostic only. No public speed or quality authority; the current boot contains an earlier GPU reset.
